title: PA TO THE CEO
company: Anderson Scott Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
PA TO THE CEO

Reading / Hybrid

Salary £32,000-£38,000

Permanent, Full Time

1 day per week in the Reading office 37.5 hours per week

The Opportunity

We are looking for an exceptionally organised, proactive and commercially aware PA to support the CEO of a growing business. This is not a traditional diary-management role.

You'll be the person who knows what needs to happen, when it needs to happen, who is responsible and what needs chasing. If you're naturally organised, commercially switched-on and confident enough to take ownership, challenge when necessary and keep things moving, this could be an excellent opportunity.

What You'll Be Doing

CEO Diary & Priorities
- Take ownership of the CEO's diary and ensure his time is used effectively.
- Manage competing demands and make sensible decisions around priorities.
- Build preparation and follow-up time into the diary.
- Identify clashes, pressure points and potential problems before they become issues.

Inbox & Action Management
- Support the CEO with a busy inbox, identifying priorities and ensuring important requests are dealt with.
- Maintain a clear list of outstanding actions, decisions and commitments.
- Follow up with senior colleagues and stakeholders to ensure deadlines are met.
- Confidently chase outstanding information and deliverables.
- Highlight anything overdue, blocked or requiring CEO intervention.

Meetings & Follow-Up
- Coordinate meetings and ensure the right people and information are in place.
- Prepare briefing information and relevant documents ahead of meetings.
- Track actions and follow up afterwards to ensure agreed outcomes happen.
- Help establish a consistent and professional approach to CEO meetings.

Reporting & Business Support
- Coordinate information and management reports from across the business.
- Ensure reporting deadlines are met and information is accurate.
- Maintain organised records and effective systems.
- Support the CEO with business and management administration.
- Identify ways to improve processes and reduce unnecessary administration.

About You

We're looking for someone who is sharp, diligent and naturally proactive.

You may currently be working as a:
- PA to a CEO, MD or senior executive
- Executive Assistant
- Senior Personal Assistant
- Office or Operations Manager with significant executive support experience

You'll be someone who:
- Takes ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do.
- Creates structure in a busy and changing environment.
- Follows things through and doesn't allow actions to disappear.
- Is confident communicating with senior people and chasing deadlines.
- Has excellent attention to detail without losing sight of the bigger picture.
- Is discreet and trustworthy when dealing with confidential information.
- Has strong commercial awareness and understands the pressures of running a business.
- Remains calm and organised when priorities change.
- Has excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Is highly confident with Microsoft Office, email, calendars and business systems and able to learn new technology quickly.

The Personality Fit

This role will suit someone who is comfortable taking control.

You shouldn't need the CEO to tell you that something needs doing.

You'll be comfortable saying:

"You have a meeting at 2pm. You need to review this beforehand, this action is still outstanding and I've chased Sarah for an update."

You'll need the confidence to remind, challenge and push when appropriate, while having the judgement and emotional intelligence to know when to step in and when to step back.

If you enjoy being the person who brings order, structure and accountability to a busy environment, you'll thrive in this role.

What Success Looks Like

You'll know you're succeeding when:
- The CEO's diary is structured, realistic and under control.
- He is consistently prepared for important meetings.
- Actions and commitments are visible and followed through.
- Management reporting is received on time.
- Problems are identified before they reach the CEO.
- Operational detail is taken away from the CEO where appropriate.
- The CEO has more time and clarity to focus on strategic priorities and growing the business.

What's On Offer
- £32,000-£38,000 salary, depending on experience
- Hybrid working - 1 day per week in the Reading office
- Permanent, full-time position - 37.5 hours per week
- Close exposure to the CEO and senior management team
- A genuinely influential role within a growing business
- The opportunity to improve and shape how the CEO and management team operate
- A role where your organisation, judgement and initiative will have a visible impact

If you're an experienced PA or EA who wants genuine responsibility rather than simply managing a diary, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Part Time Credit Controller & Customer Collections Administrator
description:
Part time - Credit Controller / Administrator - £15-£17 per hour, Windsor based - Flexible Hours - Good railway networks and a short work from the station. Friendly working office environment.

Location: Windsor (Office Based) SL4

Hours: 2 days per week - we are flexible on days/timings - would suit a mum returner

About the Role for the Part-time Credit Controller / Administrator:

We are looking for a reliable, organised and confident Credit Controller to take ownership of our customer collections process.

This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys speaking with customers, is comfortable handling payments and can work independently with minimal supervision.

You'll be responsible for contacting customers regarding overdue payments, processing card payments securely and ensuring our debtor records remain accurate and up to date.

Main Responsibilities - Credit Control
- Contact customers by telephone regarding outstanding balances.
- Chase overdue invoices professionally and courteously.
- Take secure card payments over the telephone using Worldpay.
- Record detailed notes of all customer conversations.
- Update customer accounts in QuickBooks.
- Monitor overdue accounts and follow agreed collection procedures.
- Respond to customer payment queries.
- Escalate difficult cases to management where appropriate.
- Ensure all payments are allocated correctly.
- Help reduce debtor days and improve company cashflow.
- Maintain complete confidentiality regarding customer information.

Fleet Management Administration:
- Vehicle maintenance schedules - servicing, MOTs and other maintenance requirements.
- Monitoring allocated vehicle mileage allowances.
- Safety and compliance - including ensuring drivers respond to vehicle recalls and other required actions.
- Data and technology - including monitoring/checking GPS tracking information.
- Legality and compliance - ensuring vehicles remain appropriately taxed and insured.
- Parking fines - identifying the relevant driver and ensuring fines/notices are transferred to the driver's name and address where appropriate.

Systems Used
- QuickBooks
- Worldpay
- Microsoft Outlook
- Telephone
- Shared Collections Email Inbox

Person Specification : We are looking for someone who is:
- Friendly but confident on the telephone.
- Professional and polite.
- Highly organised.
- Reliable and dependable.
- Honest and trustworthy.
- Able to work without supervision.
- Comfortable asking customers for payment.
- Calm under pressure.
- Good at listening and problem solving.
- Computer literate.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Strong administration skills

Experience for the part-time credit controller / administrator

Ideally you'll have experience in one or more of:
- Credit control
- Accounts receivable
- Customer service
- Collections
- Telephone-based roles
- Bookkeeping or finance administration

QuickBooks experience would be an advantage but training can be provided.

Personal Qualities

We're looking for someone who:
- Takes ownership of their work.
- Has excellent initiative.
- Is mature and dependable.
- Can build rapport quickly with customers.
- Is persistent without being aggressive.
- Enjoys helping businesses improve their cashflow.
- Understands the importance of professionalism and confidentiality.

What Success Looks Like

After three months you will:
- Be confidently managing overdue accounts.
- Have built positive relationships with customers.
- Be keeping debtor records fully updated.
- Be collecting payments efficiently over the phone.
- Be helping reduce overdue debt and improve cashflow.

Salary

£15.00-£17.00 per hour, depending on experience.

We're looking for someone who treats the business as if it were their own - someone who takes pride in getting things done without needing to be micromanaged.

If this sounds like you please forward your CV immediately as we would love to hear from you.

title: Customer Service Advisor - German Speaking (fixed-term)
description:
Job Description

Just imagine bringing joy to millions of LEGO fans around the world. Now make it real.

As a member of our seasonal Customer Service Advisor team, you will be at the heart of the action, helping us support our fans during our busiest season.

That's right, helping LEGO fans is our superpower, and we love it! Every day, our award-winning Consumer & Shopper Engagement (CSE) team springs into action, working to support our consumers and fulfil our Play Promise.

Are you ready to inspire the builders of tomorrow?

If you're eager about embarking on a journey filled with creativity and problem-solving, and excel at helping others and building connections, we encourage you to apply!

About the Role:

This is a fixed term contract until 31st January 2027, with several possible start dates between June and September.

As a Customer Service Advisor, you'll be responding to LEGO fans from all corners of the world during our peak season.

We offer a competitive starting salary plus incredible benefits including a performance based/discretionary bonus of up to 10%. Full in-person training will be given with a 3-week induction followed by 2 weeks on-the job support.

We also offer 'Best of Both' - our hybrid-work approach that gives our Customer Service Advisors the flexibility to work from home up to three days per week and from the office for a minimum of two each week, after training.

We resolve millions of queries each year, covering everything from building tips to troubleshooting and tracking down those elusive rare parts. Together, we're crafting new ways to connect with fans all around the globe to make the LEGO experience unforgettable!

Why you're the perfect match

If you can keep cool when LEGO mini figures are losing their heads, then we want you on the team! You'll bring energy, compassion, and fluency in English and German .

What you'll be doing
- Respond to consumers in both English and German - spoken and written.
- Engage with consumers via phone and email. Handling a range of topics, including order and returns queries, digital and app experiences, LEGO electronics, brand information, product quality and feedback queries.
- Build strong and positive relationships with consumers in a fun and engaging manner.
- Assess and solve brick-based problems using our various tools and programs, requiring solid IT skills to support consumer requests.
- Adapt to a variety of shifts and including some weekends to ensure we provide an exceptional service.

Ready to Build Something Amazing?

If you're passionate about creating magical moments for fans everywhere, don't wait! Apply now!

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. However, please note we do amend or withdraw our jobs and reserve the right to do so at any time, including prior to any advertised closing date. So, if you're interested in this role we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

What's in it for you?

Here is what you can expect:

Family Care Leave - We offer enhanced paid leave options for those important times.

Insurances - All colleagues are covered by our life and disability insurance which provides protection and peace of mind.

Wellbeing - We want our people to feel well and thrive. We offer resources and benefits to nurture physical and mental wellbeing along with opportunities to build community and inspire creativity.

Colleague Discount - We know you'll love to build, so from day 1 you will qualify for our generous colleague discount.

Bonus - We do our best work to succeed together. When goals are reached and if eligible, you'll be rewarded through our bonus scheme.

Workplace - When you join the team you'll be assigned a primary workplace location i.e. one of our Offices, stores or factories. Our hybrid work policy means an average of 3 days per week in the office. The hiring team will discuss the policy and role eligibility with you during the recruitment process.

Children are our role models. Their curiosity, creativity and imagination inspire everything we do. We strive to create a diverse, dynamic and inclusive culture of play at the LEGO Group, where everyone feels safe, valued and they belong.

The LEGO Group is highly committed to equal employment opportunity and equal pay and seeks to encourage applicants from all backgrounds (eg. sex, gender identity or expression, race/ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, age and religion) to apply for roles in our team.

The LEGO Group is fully committed to Children's Rights and Child Wellbeing across the globe. Candidates offered positions with high engagement with children are required to take part in Child Safeguarding Background Screening, as a condition of the offer.

Thank you for sharing our global commitment to Children's Rights.

Just imagine building your dream career.

Then make it real.

Join the LEGO team today.

Our client, a leading Facilities Management service provider, is looking for an enthusiastic and highly organised Workplace Coordinator to join their team in Reading.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who takes pride in creating an exceptional workplace experience and enjoys working in a busy, customer-focused environment. You will take ownership of designated floors and surrounding areas, ensuring they are well maintained, fully operational and provide an outstanding experience for employees and visitors.

The Role

As Workplace Coordinator, you will be the key point of contact for the day-to-day workplace experience across your designated areas. Working closely with Facilities, IT, Maintenance, Cleaning and other service partners, you will ensure issues are identified, reported and resolved promptly, while maintaining excellent communication with key stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- Take full ownership of designated floors and surrounding areas, ensuring they consistently provide an excellent workplace experience.
- Collaborate closely with IT, Maintenance, Cleaning and other key departments to ensure tickets and jobs are reported, tracked and closed out in a timely manner.
- Coordinate planned works with relevant teams, ensuring activities are scheduled at times that minimise disruption and maximise customer satisfaction.
- Build and maintain excellent working relationships and communication with colleagues, clients and service partners.
- Carry out the daily management of meeting rooms, ensuring they are clean, tidy, fully operational and that AV equipment is working correctly.
- Provide on-the-ground support for meetings when required, helping to ensure they run smoothly and professionally.
- Manage stationery stock levels within print areas and ensure supplies are readily available.
- Conduct daily preventative maintenance and workplace checks across photocopiers, meeting rooms, breakout areas, kitchenettes and collaboration/think spaces.
- Act as an ambassador for Three technology applications, supporting the effective management of the floors and encouraging colleagues to make full use of the available technology.
- Support the Facilities team with the management of subcontracted services, helping to ensure agreed standards and service levels are consistently achieved.
- Identify opportunities to improve the workplace experience and proactively address issues before they impact customers.

About You

We are looking for someone who is:
- Highly organised, proactive and able to take ownership.
- Customer-focused, with a genuine passion for delivering an excellent workplace experience.
- A confident communicator who can build strong relationships across multiple teams.
- Comfortable working with a range of internal departments and external service providers.
- Practical and solutions-focused, with excellent attention to detail.
- Able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced workplace environment.
- Confident using workplace technology and systems.
- Experienced within Facilities Management, Workplace Services, Property, Hospitality or a similar customer-focused environment.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established FM service provider and play a key role in delivering a high-quality, professional and engaging workplace experience.

If you're a proactive and personable individual who enjoys being hands-on, solving problems and making a visible difference to the workplace, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to take the next step in your Facilities Management career.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in ensuring they receive a welcoming and efficient service. Youll be responsible for managing incoming queries, booking appointments, handling administrative tasks and supporting the clinical team with day-to-day operations. Key Responsibilities Provide a courteous and effective reception service to patients and visitors Answer telephone calls efficiently and direct patients to the appropriate services Manage appointment bookings, including use of triage tools and hub referrals Process patient information accurately using clinical systems Respond to E-consults and email queries in a timely and professional manner Maintain effective communication within the practice team and with external healthcare partners Support other administrative duties as needed, including filing, scanning, and managing shared mailboxes What Were Looking For Excellent communication skills verbal and written Strong organisational skills and attention to detail a must. Ability to multitask, work under pressure and prioritise workload Confident using IT systems (previous EMIS experience is an advantage) Friendly, positive and team-oriented attitude Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and professionalism Flexibility to cover annual leave and absences as required Available for shifts between the hours of 8am and 6pm

title: GP Receptionist
description: Previous GP surgery is desirable but not essential. Salary will be dependent on previous experience. Full training and support will be given. The successful applicant must have previous experience working with EMIS and be confident using the system. The successful applicant must ideally have previous GP Reception or customer service experience, with experience dealing with the general public, a good telephone manner and the ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult situations, while maintaining a firm but empathetic approach. The role involves communicating with patients face to face, by telephone, text and email, so you must enjoy working with the public and providing a high standard of patient service. Previous experience working in a GP Practice and essential EMIS experience are required for this role. The successful applicant must be confident using EMIS for booking appointments, processing blood test requests, dealing with prescription requests and patient queries, scanning documents and completing general administrative tasks. Excellent IT and organisational skills are essential, along with the ability to multitask and work effectively in a busy environment. Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Outlook and Word, is also required. Receptionist / Administrator Job Description Essential Experience and Skills: The successful applicant must have previous experience using EMIS in a GP practice setting. Applicants without previous EMIS experience will not be considered. The successful applicant will ideally have previous NHS/GP reception or administrative experience and will be confident dealing with patients both face to face and via telephone, email and other communication methods. Previous experience using EMIS in a GP practice is essential Previous NHS or GP practice reception/administrative experience Excellent customer service and communication skills A professional and friendly telephone manner Ability to communicate effectively with patients, carers, GPs and other healthcare professionals Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, email and internet applications Ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult or challenging situations Excellent organisational skills and the ability to multitask Ability to manage workload effectively and work to deadlines Flexible, enthusiastic and reliable approach to work Self-confidence, energy, determination and perseverance Ability to work effectively as part of a team Willingness and ability to provide cover for holidays and sickness High level of confidentiality, integrity and professionalism The post-holder will be responsible for providing an efficient and professional reception and administrative service to patients and the practice team. Duties will include: Booking, cancelling and rearranging patient appointments via EMIS, telephone, face to face and email Using EMIS effectively to access and update patient records and undertake relevant administrative tasks Processing prescription requests in accordance with practice procedures Handling patient enquiries and requests appropriately and efficiently Responding to telephone calls, emails and face-to-face enquiries Liaising with GPs, practice staff, hospitals and other community healthcare providers Handling requests from patients and GPs and ensuring these are directed to the appropriate member of the team Signposting patients to appropriate services where required Processing correspondence and administrative tasks accurately Maintaining accurate and up-to-date patient information Ensuring all work is completed in accordance with practice policies and procedures Supporting colleagues and providing reception cover when required The post-holder will strive to maintain high standards of quality within the practice and will: Alert team members to issues relating to quality, safety and risk Take responsibility for their own performance and actions Contribute positively to team effectiveness and suggest improvements to practice processes Work effectively with colleagues and external healthcare providers to meet patients' needs Manage their own time, workload and resources effectively Participate in relevant audits and quality improvement activities where appropriate Follow practice policies, procedures, standards and clinical guidance relevant to the role The post-holder will have access to confidential and sensitive information relating to patients, carers, practice staff, healthcare professionals and the practice as a business. All information must be treated as strictly confidential and handled in accordance with practice policies, confidentiality requirements and current data protection legislation. Information may only be shared with authorised individuals and in accordance with practice procedures. The post-holder will: Comply with the practice's health and safety and infection prevention and control policies Complete all mandatory training relevant to the role Maintain a safe, clean and tidy working environment Identify and report health and safety or infection control risks promptly Follow appropriate procedures to minimise risks to patients, visitors and staff Use workplace security systems appropriately Maintain high standards of cleanliness within reception, administrative and patient-facing areas Report hazards and take appropriate corrective action where required The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues by: Treating everyone with dignity, respect and professionalism Respecting patients' privacy, dignity, needs, beliefs and individual circumstances Providing a welcoming, non-judgemental and inclusive service Recognising and responding appropriately to individual communication needs Working in accordance with practice policies and current equality and diversity legislation Participate in training relevant to the role and the running of the practice Complete mandatory and role-specific training within required timescales Participate in an annual performance review Take responsibility for maintaining their own knowledge, skills and development Identify learning needs and undertake relevant training Share knowledge and good practice with colleagues where appropriate Effective communication is an essential part of the role. The post-holder will: Communicate clearly and professionally with patients, carers, colleagues, GPs and other healthcare professionals Maintain a professional and empathetic approach when dealing with patients Recognise individual communication needs and adapt communication accordingly Ensure messages and requests are recorded and passed to the appropriate person accurately Contribute to improving communication within the practice The post-holder will work closely with external healthcare providers and organisations, including: Hospitals and outpatient departments Other GP practices Community healthcare services Other NHS and healthcare providers They will ensure requests and information are communicated accurately and efficiently and that appropriate follow-up action is taken where required. The post-holder is expected to work flexibly as part of the practice team and undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. The above job description is not exhaustive and may be reviewed and amended in line with the needs of the practice. Previous hands-on experience using EMIS within a GP practice is essential for this role. Candidates who do not have EMIS experience will not be shortlisted.
